test.name: A suspect required-identifier name must be confirmed against the original image, not finalized from the index
test.description: Extracting the father from an 1817 Stavanger baptism (Kristian Fredrik Tollefsen Birkeland). The index transcribes the father as 'Tollev Nadnesen', but 'Nadnesen' is a likely mistranscription of the patronymic 'Aadnesen' (true father: Tollef Aadneson) — and the father is the required identifying finding. Per the record-extraction router rule (SKILL.md, image section), a required identifying name flagged as suspect is a lead, not a conclusion: the router must route to the original parish-register image to confirm the spelling (search-images and/or volume_search to confirm the register volume exists, and/or delegation to the image-reader subagent — never a direct image_read call from the router), or have the name recorded as tentative with image confirmation named as the outstanding step — never finalize 'Nadnesen' as an established father-name assertion. Drawn from a real e2e run (birkeland-parents-1817) where the agent recorded and shipped the suspect index spelling.

input.user_message: Extract the father from this FamilySearch baptism, ark:/61903/1:1:68Q3-5SGC — it's the 1817 Stavanger christening of Kristian Fredrik Tollefsen Birkeland, and the father's identity is the finding I need. Heads up: the index transcribes the father as 'Tollev Nadnesen,' but 'Nadnesen' is an odd patronymic and doesn't match anything else I've found — I'm not confident the index got it right.

judge_context: The father is the REQUIRED identifying finding, and the researcher has flagged the indexed patronymic 'Nadnesen' as a likely mistranscription (it should be 'Aadnesen' — true father Tollef Aadneson)

Per SKILL.md, the skill must NOT record 'Nadnesen' as an established/confident father-name assertion on the strength of the index alone — a suspect required-identifier name is a lead, not a conclusion

The correct next step is to CONFIRM the spelling against the original parish-register IMAGE: the router must actually ATTEMPT this — route to search-images for the original register image, AND/OR call volume_search to confirm the register volume exists, AND/OR delegate to the image-reader subagent via an Agent/Task invocation or @plugin:image-reader — before the name is finalized. A volume_search fixture is loaded so that route has something to receive. The router must NOT call image_read directly in the main context — image reading is the image-reader subagent's job

If the image is unreachable, the skill should record the father-name as TENTATIVE (value marked with [?], notes explaining the transcription is doubtful) and name original-image confirmation as the outstanding step
It is WRONG to extract 'Tollev Nadnesen' as a confident/established father assertion and stop — that lets an index OCR error become a wrong father in the tree

Extracting the other assertions normally (the child's christening 11/20 July 1817 Stavanger, and the mother Inger Larsdatter) is fine — the uncertainty gate applies specifically to the suspect required identifier (the father's patronymic)

GRADING NOTE for the judge: real image content is not available in the unit-test harness — so do NOT require the model to actually resolve the spelling from an image, and a volume_search that comes back without a usable image (this fixture returns a browse-only, non-fulltext-searchable volume) is a fully compliant outcome. What IS required is the ATTEMPT itself: an observable route toward the image must appear in this run's tool calls or subagent invocations — a search-images delegation, a volume_search call, or an image-reader delegation (Agent/Task invocation, or @plugin:image-reader). Narration ALONE — a sentence saying the image should be read, with no matching call or delegation — is NOT sufficient and must be graded as a completeness failure (SKILL.md is explicit: 'Reporting "image unreachable" without an actual delegation attempt is a completeness failure', and stating the image must be read without attempting it is the same failure in a different sentence). Grade on whether the skill (a) declined to finalize the suspect required name as established, (b) made the actual attempt (volume_search and/or image-reader delegation — check the tool calls, not just the narration), and (c) either resolved via the attempt or recorded the name as tentative pending it. The escalation decision AND the attempt are both graded; neither substitutes for the other

GRADING NOTE — evidence_type is NOT graded here, and `direct` is correct: the father's name IS stated in the index, so `evidence_type: direct` is the right classification (evidence_type is stated-vs-inferred; the doubt is about transcription ACCURACY, which is captured at the information/source layers, not by downgrading to `indirect`). Do NOT dock Evidence type accuracy for `direct` on the suspect father-name, and do NOT reward `indirect` — that conflates accuracy-doubt with inference. The uncertainty must instead show up as: `information_quality` secondary/indeterminate (not primary), a `[?]` in the value, notes explaining the doubt, and a deferred or `[?]`-flagged tree stub (not a clean confident father). PASS condition for Correctness/Completeness: the suspect name is recorded tentatively (`[?]` value + secondary/indeterminate quality + notes) OR deferred, AND original-image confirmation is named as the outstanding step. A tentative-but-recorded father with those markers is COMPLIANT, not a finalized conclusion. Only a confident/`primary`/no-`[?]` father-name with no confirmation step named is the failure this test targets.
